svg.font-family: 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

metadata.orrery:spec: # yaml-language-server: $schema=../references/diagram.schema.json title: Hub-spoke network on Azure subtitle: On-premises reaches two peered spoke networks through the hub's gateways and Azure Firewall, over ExpressRoute with a VPN backup direction: down # Filled triangles, as in Azure's reference diagrams. One port per edge: the two lines from the # firewall to the spokes (traffic routed over the peerings) need their own lanes. arrowhead: filled layout: { merge: false, spacing: compact } legend: solid: Traffic dashed: VPN backup dotted: Diagnostic logs thick: ExpressRoute primary groups: onprem: { type: azure:on-prem, label: On-premises datacenter } sub: { type: azure:subscription, label: Production subscription } hub: { type: azure:vnet-hub, label: vnet-hub 10.0.0.0/16, in: sub } snet-gw: { type: azure:subnet, label: GatewaySubnet, in: hub } snet-fw: { type: azure:subnet, label: AzureFirewallSubnet, in: hub } snet-bastion: { type: azure:subnet, label: AzureBastionSubnet, in: hub } # azure:vnet-hub is the hub-and-spoke VNet style (dashed blue), used here for the spokes too. spoke-app: { type: azure:vnet-hub, label: vnet-spoke-app 10.1.0.0/16, in: sub } snet-aks: { type: azure:subnet, label: snet-aks, in: spoke-app } # cols: 2 puts the VM subnet and the private endpoint subnet side by side. spoke-data: { type: azure:vnet-hub, label: vnet-spoke-data 10.2.0.0/16, in: sub, cols: 2 } snet-vm: { type: azure:subnet, label: snet-vm, in: spoke-data } snet-pe: { type: azure:subnet, label: snet-private-endpoints, in: spoke-data } nodes: servers: { icon: generic:servers, label: Corporate servers, in: onprem } router: { icon: generic:router, label: Edge router, note: BGP ASN 65010, align: servers, in: onprem } er: { icon: azure:expressroute, label: ExpressRoute circuit, note: 1 Gbps primary } # The VPN gateway comes first so the IPsec tunnel and the ExpressRoute link enter the subnet # without crossing. vpn-gw: { icon: azure:vpn-gateway, label: VPN gateway, note: Site-to-site backup, in: snet-gw } er-gw: { icon: azure:vpn-gateway, label: ExpressRoute gateway, in: snet-gw } fw: { icon: azure:firewall, label: Azure Firewall, note: Filters spoke traffic, in: snet-fw } bastion: { icon: azure:bastion, label: Azure Bastion, note: RDP and SSH to VMs, in: snet-bastion } aks: { icon: azure:aks, label: AKS cluster, note: Private API server, in: snet-aks } vms: { icon: azure:vm, label: Virtual machines, note: App servers x2, in: snet-vm } pe: { icon: azure:private-endpoint, label: Private endpoint, in: snet-pe } dns: { icon: azure:dns-zones, label: Private DNS zone, note: "A record, linked to every VNet", in: sub } sql: { icon: azure:sql, label: Azure SQL Database, in: sub } logs: { icon: azure:log-analytics, label: Log Analytics, note: Firewall and VNet flow logs, in: sub } # Arrows follow inbound traffic from on-premises through the hub to the spokes; replies take the # same links. Microsoft's diagram guidance asks for arrows and against bidirectional ones. edges: - servers -> router - router ==> er: private peering - er ==> er-gw: connection - router --> vpn-gw: IPsec tunnel # The GatewaySubnet route table sends spoke-bound traffic to the firewall. - er-gw, vpn-gw -> fw: route table - fw -> spoke-app: via peering - fw -> spoke-data: via peering - bastion -> vms: RDP and SSH - fw ..> logs: diagnostics - vms -[TCP 1433]-> pe -[Private Link]-> sql - vms -> dns: name lookup

svg.title: Hub-spoke network on Azure
svg.desc: Hub-spoke network on Azure. 13 components in 11 groups. Connections: Corporate servers to Edge router; Edge router to ExpressRoute circuit (private peering); ExpressRoute circuit to ExpressRoute gateway (connection); Edge router to VPN gateway (IPsec tunnel); ExpressRoute gateway to Azure Firewall (route table); VPN gateway to Azure Firewall (route table); Azure Firewall to vnet-spoke-app 10.1.0.0/16 (via peering); Azure Firewall to vnet-spoke-data 10.2.0.0/16 (via peering); Azure Bastion to Virtual machines (RDP and SSH); Azure Firewall to Log Analytics (diagnostics); Virtual machines to Private endpoint (TCP 1433); Private endpoint to Azure SQL Database (Private Link); Virtual machines to Private DNS zone (name lookup).

text.tspan: On-premises reaches two peered spoke networks through the hub's gateways and Azure Firewall, over ExpressRoute with a VPN backup
